engine.meaning: The facts are all there because the text is nearly verbatim ("When thick foods are cooked, the outer layers are heated and cooked primarily by microwaves"), but the grammar breaks in places ("because tucker cook faster", "tucker cooked in a microwave oven may keep more of their vitamins"). Interjections "Bloody hell" and "Bugger me" add nothing.
engine.sense: "tucker" is swapped in mechanically for every "food", including technical claims ("does not make tucker “radioactive” or "contaminated.""), where it reads oddly; "people's mitts and faces" in a serious burn report strains. "alfoil" and "veggies" fit.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: "Bloody hell, the microwaves are reflected within the metal interior of the oven where they are absorbed by tucker." and "Bugger me, Super-heated water" are bolted onto untouched bureaucratic prose. US "spoon full" left in.
engine.register: Apart from word swaps and two swears, it is the original FDA text ("Users should closely follow the precautions and recommendations provided"), far lighter than a level-3 retelling; the swearing is within dad level.
engine.tone: The calm informational tone wobbles at "Bugger me, Super-heated water", which makes the safety warning sound flippant.
engine.flow: Jarring joins and repetition: "absorbed by tucker, and does not make tucker", "because tucker cook faster", "Bugger me, Super-heated water".
engine.variety: "tucker" eleven-odd times; nothing else but "veggies", "mitts", "alfoil" and two swears.
engine.essence: Recognisably the FDA explainer because it is barely changed, but flattened by the tucker refrain and stray swears.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives: the magnetron, reflection, water molecules, "microwaves don't cook food from the "inside out."", conduction from outer layers, nutrition, containers, metal and foil, super-heating and the advice on heating times.
unharnessed.sense: "jiggle about" for vibrate, "knock the goodness out of food" for reduce nutritional value, "you might wreck the oven" for damage, "cuts that risk right down"; all fit.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain Australian: "Fact is, food done in the microwave might hang on to more of its vitamins", "tipping in a spoonful of instant coffee". "Folks should stick closely" is American.
unharnessed.register: A level-3 conversational retelling ("your tucker", "veggies", "alfoil", "nasty skin burns") without overdoing it; no swearing, fine for the dad limit.
unharnessed.tone: Stays informative and serious about the burns ("nasty skin burns and scalds on people's hands and faces"), just friendlier.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "They bounce around the metal insides of the oven till the food soaks them up."
unharnessed.variety: "jiggle about", "soaks them up", "knock the goodness out", "hang on to", "wreck", "tipping in", "cuts that risk right down".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the FDA microwave explainer, structure and safety section intact, including the heading.

yarn.meaning: All points kept, from "an electron tube called a magnetron" to "make sure you don't go over the recommended heatin' times". "flamin' violent eruption" is colour.
yarn.sense: "jigglin' about", "knock the goodness out of food", "you could stuff up the oven", "bustin' out of a cup", "cuts the risk right down"; all fit.
yarn.authenticity: Natural: "you could stuff up the oven", "If it's gone super-heated", "heaps of water". The dropped g's ("Cookin' in the microwave can use less energy than cookin' the usual way") are a little laid on for an instruction text.
yarn.register: Level 3 with a bit of extra drawl in spelling ("Microwavin'", "heatin' times", "boilin' point"), and one mild intensifier "flamin'"; a touch heavier than asked but close.
yarn.tone: Informative and still serious about burns ("bad skin burns and scalds on people's hands and faces"); "flamin' violent eruption" is emphatic, not flippant.
yarn.flow: Smooth overall; slight redundancy in "they can still get hot from the hot food cookin' inside", and the apostrophes pile up ("pickin' up the cup or tippin' in a spoonful").
yarn.variety: "jigglin' about", "heaps", "knock the goodness out", "hang on to", "stuff up", "bustin' out", "tippin' in"; varied, though the dropped-g device recurs constantly.
yarn.essence: Clearly the FDA explainer, with the safety heading retold ("Not Gettin' Hurt by Super-Heated Water in the Microwave").
